content.text: Section 12 gives our client the broad convenience right and gives Harpoon none. This sits within the fallback.

input.quote: 12.3 Additional Termination Rights by AbbVie. AbbVie may terminate this Agreement in its entirety, or on a country or other jurisdiction -by-country or other jurisdiction basis, for any or no reason, upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Harpoon.
input.rationale: Section 12.3 gives us (AbbVie, the customer/licensee) an unqualified termination-for-convenience right — "for any or no reason" — exercisable either in its entirety or country-by-country on ninety (90) days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, break payment or other penalty anywhere in Article 12. Harpoon has no convenience right at all: its termination rights are confined to material breach (12.2.1), failure of Commercialization diligence in a Major Market (12.2.2, and only as to the affected Major Market) and insolvency (12.4), each mutual and cure-protected. This sits at the playbook fallback (customer termination on 60–90 days' notice, no fee, no vendor convenience right) rather than the preferred 30 days' notice, so it is acceptable and we do not redline it. Noted but not flagged: (i) notice is 90 days rather than the preferred 30, and (ii) termination under 12.3 triggers reversion of the Licensed Compounds/Products to Harpoon under 12.6.1 and 12.7 plus a sell-off period whose length Harpoon sets in its sole discretion (12.10.2) — these are ordinary reversion consequences of a development/option licence, not a monetary penalty on our exit, and 12.10.1 preserves accrued rights only. There are no prepaid subscription fees to refund in this structure, so the pro-rata refund mechanic is inapplicable.
